Scuderia Ferrari.summary: Ferrari has added a small winglet to the halo pillar, a tweak that helps manage airflow and reduces the load on the driver’s protective halo during high‑speed corners. The extra aerodynamic bite should tighten the car’s front balance, giving the driver a bit more grip and stability when pushing hard this weekend. In short, it’s a subtle aero boost aimed at shaving off a few tenths of a second per lap.

Racing Bulls / RB.summary: Racing Bulls have tweaked the shape of the little winglets on the rear brake ducts, smoothing the airflow around the car’s rear corner. The change should give a steadier rear‑end grip and a tiny boost in straight‑line speed, helping the car stay stable through high‑speed corners. In short, it’s a modest aerodynamic lift that could translate into a few extra tenths of a second around the track this weekend.

Haas F1 Team.summary: Haas has tweaked the rear‑impact area of the car, stiffening the structure where the rear suspension meets the chassis. That change sharpens the car’s handling and gives the drivers a more predictable feel through the fast corners this weekend. In short, it’s a small but crucial upgrade aimed at squeezing a little extra pace and confidence out of the package.

Audi F1 Team.summary: Audi’s F1 car gets a fresh front wing and a reshaped nose, both tweaked to give the front end more grip and stability as the car charges into corners. The new wing profile smooths airflow and the revised nose cuts turbulence, translating into quicker turn‑ins and better balance on the circuit. In short, the car should feel more planted and responsive, giving the drivers a tangible edge right from the start line.

Cadillac.summary: Cadillac’s new updates trim the airflow at the rear and tidy up the side‑mirror brackets – the diffuser winglets now have a refined edge and the mirror stay’s front surface is slightly reshaped. Those tweaks shave off a bit of drag and improve stability, giving the car a cleaner‑sweeping rear end and steadier handling through high‑speed corners. In short, the changes should translate into a tighter pack‑run and a better shot at defending position this weekend.
